record.final_answer:
Short answer: not with polling; yes with push streaming. The blocker is plan tier and connection plumbing, not latency.

Why polling can't do it
Nimbrel server SDK 4.x polls for flag rules every 30 s by default, and the polling interval cannot be set below 10 s (vendor docs, docs.nimbrel.example/sdk/updates, read 2026-04-20). A flip therefore lands at a random point in the poll cycle: even tuned to the 10 s minimum, worst case is ~10 s plus request time, before the console write has even propagated to the flag service. A 5 s promise isn't deliverable on polling, and "5 s on average" isn't what product is asking for.

What does hit 5 s
Push updates: set stream: true in the client options, and the SDK receives changes when they happen instead of discovering them on a timer. Available on Team plan and above only.

What it would take
1. Plan check or upgrade to Team+ for the relevant environment. That gates everything — confirm it before scoping engineering.
2. SDK 4.x with stream: true on every service that evaluates flags, keeping polling configured as fallback so a dropped stream degrades to 10 s rather than stale flags indefinitely.
3. Survivable connections end to end: long-lived streams through ingress, load balancers and any service mesh; idle timeouts raised (>= 60 s with heartbeats), response buffering off, SSE/HTTP2 confirmed at every hop. Anything that buffers or aggressively recycles connections breaks push silently.
4. Reconnect logic: backoff with jitter, a watchdog that re-subscribes, and a forced poll on reconnect to close the gap. Log stream gaps so misses are visible.
5. Capacity review: one persistent connection per instance — check the flag service's / plan's concurrent stream limit against peak instance count, autoscaling spikes included.
6. No hidden cache delay: any in-process flag cache TTL must fit inside the 5 s budget or be invalidated on stream events.
7. Short-lived or serverless workloads can't hold a stream. For those, 5 s means evaluating flags per request in a service that does hold the stream, or adding your own push channel (pub/sub) — materially bigger than a client-option flip.
8. Measurement: record console-write time vs. flag-applied time per service, dashboard the p99, alert above 5 s. The budget includes console -> flag-service propagation, not just SDK delivery.

Caveats
Push is best-effort delivery, not a transactional guarantee: instances that are disconnected, reconnecting or partitioned will miss the 5 s window. If product means a hard guarantee, the answer is per-request evaluation, not SDK streaming.

Two things I couldn't verify from here: our current SDK version/plan tier, and whether the services are long-running — the workspace repo is an empty initial commit, so there was nothing local to check. The doc fact is also dated 2026-04-20, so worth re-confirming against current docs before committing to a date.
